seo.og_title: Parc Lalla Aicha, Oujda: Green Park & Family Tips
seo.og_description: Oujda’s green lung – a 1930s park with trees, fountains and a relaxed local atmosphere ideal for a break from the medina.

name: Parc Lalla Aicha
hero_subtitle: Oujda’s favourite green space: shaded walks, fountains and a calm family atmosphere designed in the 1930s.

overview.title: A Green Pause in the City
overview.p1: Parc Lalla Aicha (sometimes also referred to in connection with Lalla Meryem gardens) is the main public park in central Oujda. Designed in the 1930s, it offers tree-lined paths, flower beds, fountains and open spaces where local families gather, especially in the late afternoon and evening.
overview.p2: It is not a botanical spectacle like some famous gardens further west; it is a working urban park. That is its charm. You come here to slow down, sit in the shade, watch children play and feel the everyday rhythm of the city away from traffic and souks.
overview.p3: A visit pairs naturally with the medina in the morning and the park in the cooler hours, or as a quiet interlude between other city sights.

moods.title: When to Enjoy the Park
moods.subtitle: The park changes character with the light and the temperature.

1.title: Quiet and Fresh
1.desc: Fewer people, cooler air and soft light for photos. Ideal if you want a peaceful start before the medina heats up.

2.title: Local Life at Its Best
2.desc: Families arrive, children play, the light turns warm. This is when the park feels most alive and most Oujda.

3.title: Cooler Air and Conversation
3.desc: After sunset the temperature drops and groups stay to talk. A gentle end to a city day before dinner.

food.title: What to Eat Near the Park
food.p1: The park itself is for walking and resting. Food is found in the surrounding streets and toward the centre.
food.li1: Nearby cafés for mint tea, coffee and simple pastries.
food.li2: Karan and barida a short walk away in the direction of the medina or main avenues.
food.li3: Small restaurants serving grills and daily specials.
food.li4: Ice cream and soft drinks sold around the park entrances in warmer months.
food.li5: For a fuller meal, continue to Place du 16 Août or the modern centre.
food.p2: Bring water if you plan to stay a while, especially in summer. Shade is plentiful but the heat can still build.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Parc Lalla Aicha

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: The park is central and easy to reach by petit taxi or on foot from many hotels. Ask for “Parc Lalla Aicha” – drivers know it well.

2.title: Best For
2.desc: Families, anyone needing a break from walking, and travellers who want to see local life without entering a commercial space.

3.title: Practical Notes
3.desc: Wear comfortable shoes. Keep an eye on belongings in busier evening hours. The park is generally very safe and frequented by families.

q1.question: Is Parc Lalla Aicha free?
q1.answer: Access is free or requires only a very small symbolic fee depending on the entrance and season. There is no expensive ticket.

q2.question: What is the best time to visit?
q2.answer: Late afternoon into early evening, when local families arrive and the light is softer. Morning is quieter if you prefer fewer people.

q3.question: Is the park suitable for children?
q3.answer: Yes. It is one of the best places in central Oujda for families. Open spaces and a relaxed atmosphere make it easy to spend time with kids.

q4.question: How long should I stay?
q4.answer: 45 minutes to 1.5 hours is typical. Longer if you simply want to sit, read or let children play.

q5.question: Can I combine it with the medina on the same day?
q5.answer: Easily. Visit the medina in the cooler morning hours, then come to the park when the heat builds or in the late afternoon.
